info.name: E-commerce API
info.description:
Week 1 e-commerce API. One collection for both frameworks: pick the **Express** or **NestJS** environment (top right).

**Before the first run:** start the server and run `npm run db:seed` (it creates the admin).

**How it works**
- Collection auth is `Bearer {{customerToken}}`. Admin requests override it with `{{adminToken}}`; public ones use No Auth. Check each request's **Authorization** tab.
- **Register** and the **Login** requests save tokens and ids to the environment. Later requests reuse them (`{{productId}}`, `{{categoryId}}`, ...).
- A collection pre-request script logs in again when a token is missing or about to expire.
- Every request has tests (**Test Results** tab). A collection-level test checks that every error uses `{ "error": { "code" } }`.
- **Run the whole thing:** right-click the collection, then **Run**. Folders run top to bottom and can be re-run.
- **See the raw traffic:** View, then Console.

exec: // Runs before every request. Logs in again when a saved token is missing or about to expire
// (tokens last 1 hour), so you never have to re-run Login by hand.
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email, password }) },
// House rule for both frameworks: every error body looks like { "error": { "code": ... } }.

item.name: Cart
item.description: Every cart route needs a login (collection auth: the customer token). The user comes from the token, so there is no user id in any URL.

request.description: PUT sets the quantity (it does not add to it), so sending it twice gives the same cart.
Idempotent: still 2, not 4.

item.name: Set quantity: more than in stock (409)
Orders
item.description: Checkout turns the cart into an order inside one transaction: stock goes down with a conditional update, prices are copied into the order, and the cart is emptied. Any failure rolls all of it back. Uses a seeded product (Stardew Valley) for the order, and the Postman Gadget for the out-of-stock case.

request.description: Looks up a seeded product and saves `orderProductId` and its current `orderProductStock`.

exec: pm.test('found a product with at least 2 in stock', () => pm.expect(p.stock).to.be.at.least(2));

request.description: Checkout. Takes no body: the order is built from the cart. Saves `orderId`. Each line keeps `unitPriceCents`, the price at the time of the order.

request.description: The admin token belongs to a different user. Orders are looked up by id **and** the user from the token, so this is a 404: the API does not even confirm the order exists.
Only a PENDING order can be cancelled. Its stock goes back in the same transaction.
The status check is part of the update (`WHERE status = PENDING`), so stock can never be returned twice.
